reviewer: owner.lisp:5745-5768: the install, the swap and fnn-owner-reclaim-barriers all run in a bare fnn-owner-gated. The macro at 1573-1605 neither fences nor checks STOPPING, and the body is not wrapped in fnn-owner-shared-action-locked. On fnn-os-error, reclaim-barriers raises fnn-indeterminate (5615-5619). The call chain is admin.lisp:577 to fnn-owner-reclaim-request to fnn-owner-reclaim-pass (admin.lisp:437). control.lisp:369-372 then logs 'owner fenced' and answers :uncertain, but nothing called stop-service. (b) is also true: in the cleanup at 5792-5798, the indeterminate raise when installed and not swapped comes before the orcp-finish form, so finish is skipped and nothing stops the service. (c) is also true: fnn-owner-gated never checks STOPPING, so the swap quantum can install after a fence. The triggers are rare (EIO or an ACL2 swap fault during a reclaim), so severity is medium.
scenario: (a) The checkpoint is installed and the owner, catalog and history are swapped, then a recovery barrier gets an fnn-os-error. fnn-indeterminate propagates out of the gated body, which never calls fnn-owner-stop-service-locked. The control handler logs 'owner fenced' and answers :uncertain, but STOPPING is nil and the node keeps serving a swapped owner that is not :ready. Per the comment at 5606-5607, every later POST then waits forever. (b) fn-owner-orcp-swap faults after fnn-state-checkpoint-install. The cleanup raises 'recovery required' outside any lock, no stop happens, and the old state is served over a new durable publication. The raise also skips fn-owner-orcp-finish, so every later `store reclaim` answers :in-flight. (c) fnn-owner-gated never checks STOPPING, so a pass already past capture still installs a new checkpoint after an uncertain batch fenced the store at exit 3.
title: Reclaim recovery events are raised from unfenced gated bodies and cleanup: the control reply says 'owner fenced' while the node keeps serving
